items.title: Sustainable AI: Tools, frameworks and best practices in 2026
items.summary: Sustainability professionals are scrambling to understand how AI adoption will impact environmental goals.

items.title: The hidden water liability of AI data centers
items.summary: Data centers are thirstier than most people realize, but not because of the water pumped into their on-site cooling equipment.

items.title: New rules let PepsiCo integrate emissions certificates into its carbon accounts
items.summary: When the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) said in June that it would give companies more flexibility in tackling supply-chain emissions, the decision won applause from businesses that have been struggling to shrink that part of their footprint.

items.title: Two data centres set to emit more than ExxonMobil’s UK operations, analysis warns
items.summary: Two upcoming data centres will emit 4.5 million tonnes of carbon a year when fully running, analysis by non-profit Foxglove has found, exceeding fossil fuel company ExxonMobil’s entire UK emissions.

items.title: How AI can accelerate investment in climate solutions
items.summary: Event Date: 27/10/2026 | 1:00 pm UK | 9:00 am US East Coast ET | 6:00 am US West Coast PT | 2:00 pm Central Europe CET/CEST Join the edie webinar masterclass on 27 October 2026 to discover how AI can significantly boost investment in vital climate solutions.

items.title: Study: Climate damage costs from North Sea oil and gas would outweigh productivity boost
items.summary: As more North Sea projects are successfully decommissioned, new research has found that the economic value that the Jackdaw and Rosebank oil and gas fields could bring could be lost six times over due to increased climate damage.

items.title: The EU Circular Economy Act could supercharge circular electronics – if it’s built for scale
items.summary: The EU’s upcoming Circular Economy Act (CEA) has a chance to deliver circularity for electronics, but only if it creates the economic, technological and regulatory conditions that enable circularity at scale, argues Global Electronics Association's director of sustainability policy, Dr Diana Radovan.

items.title: COP17 advances tools to boost global drought resilience
items.summary: On the conference's dedicated Water Day (26 August), nations announced new progress on global water security, including a pooled fund for vulnerable countries, catalytic financing for drought resilience and the first Drought Resilience Index.

items.title: ‘Like patching a leaking pipe’: Energy cap rise sparks calls for reform
items.summary: Today (26 August), Ofgem confirmed a 4% increase on October's energy price cap, bringing bills to a three-year high.

items.title: ONS: Heat linked to more than 40,000 deaths in England since 1988
items.summary: The cold has long been the silent killer. But the data now tells a different story, one where the warmth is claiming more lives than previously understood.
